content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @sam @maria @derek — elevated GPU driver-reset rate observed in us-west-2-infer pool (nodes inf-gpu-0*). 42 resets in last 5m, multiple pods restarting. Auto-evac policies firing.

sam: seeing it. logs show repeated NV driver soft resets, containers OOM'ing shortly after restart. tagging oncall.

maria: grabbing telemetry now, pulling dmesg + nvidia-smi. please hold any non-urgent deploys to that pool.

derek: quick sanity: are these coming from same driver version? I saw a rolling kernel update earlier today.

eve: confirmed same driver across nodes, but kernel patchlevel differs on 3 hosts (inf-gpu-07/09/11). possible ABI skew.

sam: next steps — 1) cordon the most noisy nodes, 2) scale up fallback CPU workers for critical routes, 3) flip routing to secondary region if customer impact > 5%.

maria: compiling logs:

```
# dmesg | tail -n 30
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid 116: 0x00000000
[  123.456792] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.456795] kernel: nv-host-reset: reset triggered
[  124.001234] docker: container exited with code 137 (OOM)
```

maria: nvidia-smi snapshot shows ECC correctable spikes and memory utilization steady ~95% on affected GPUs. attaching short csv to thread.

ops-bot: autoscaler: launched 6 x c5.4xlarge fallback instances for critical-service, expected ready in ~90s.

sam: cordoning inf-gpu-07 and inf-gpu-11 (most resets). running `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` with graceful 120s.

derek: FYI I see kernel oops traces referencing a parity check path — not the usual Xid 79 pattern. might be ECC parity flicker.

maria: customer impact so far: 12% error rate on /v1/generate for the last 20m for customers pinned to us-west-2 pool; latency p50 up 2.8x. marking impact: partial degrade.

sam: initiating partial failover for high-qps customers. routing rule 'route:fallback-on-driver' set to prefer us-east by weight 0.6.

eve: running a quick live mitigation: reduce per-request max_seq from 2048->1024 to drop memory pressure; applying gencfg profile change to runtime-params on affected nodepool.

maria: logs after throttling: still seeing resets but frequency halved. memory reclaim looks better.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary CPU fallback accepted, %requests routed to CPU fallback = 18%.

derek: i'm going to reimage inf-gpu-09 (closest to kernel skew) and reprovision driver 535.86 across the three mixed nodes. will rotate one at a time.

sam: agree, but keep at most 1 node down from the pool at once. we want graceful draining.

maria: opening short customer note draft: "We're investigating increased driver resets in our us-west GPU pool causing elevated errors for a subset of requests. Mitigations are in place; routing and memory-limits adjusted. We'll update in 30m." thoughts? :speech_balloon:

eve: +1, add that we've started node rotation and that larger customers can request manual region pinning.

derek: reimage started on inf-gpu-09. reprovision script snippet:

```
#!/bin/bash
sudo systemctl stop inference-agent
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535=535.86-0
sudo reboot
```

sam: monitoring: airtime. dashboards show error-traffic clustering on the same 4 instance-ids. if repro succeeds on 09, we'll roll 07/11 as well.

maria: telemetry after reimage (inf-gpu-09) — 09 stable for 7m, no resets. inf-gpu-07 still noisy.

incident-bot: severity update -> SEV2 (partial degraded multi-tenant impact). owners: sam (oncall), derek (node rotation), maria (telemetry & customer comms).

sam: handoff to next oncall in 25m. @eve will you cover during rotation of 07/11?

eve: I can. i'll watch the routing weight rollback plan if things go sideways.

maria: customer note updated and queued. posting to status.redwood.ai in 10m.

derek: rolling 07 now. starting drain -> reprovision -> join. keeping drain grace at 120s.

sam: heads up — if we still see resets post-reprovision, we may need to force-evacuate the pool and escalate to HW vendor; prepare support bundle with /var/log/nvidia*.

ops-bot: note: kvcache mempressure logs show transient spikes correlated with long sequences. consider enforcing shorter sequence cap for best-effort tenants.

maria: summary for postmortem: likely root cause = combined kernel-driver ABI skew + ECC parity bursts under high-seq workloads; immediate mitigations = node rotation, seq cap, routing failover.

sam: ok, handoff checklist: - confirm inf-gpu-07 stable after reprovision - monitor error rate <3% for 20m - leave feature flags in place (seq cap + routing) until postmortem.

eve: acknowledged. i'll pick this up and add notes to the incident runbook.

maria: posting final update to channel after we see 20m stable window. good work folks. :thumbsup:"
